answer.text:
Official key A checked; editorial worked explanation:

For the isolated system of the two colliding objects, the internal collision forces are equal and opposite, so the total momentum is conserved when external impulse is negligible. Because the collision is inelastic, some of the initial kinetic energy is transferred to internal energy, deformation or sound, so kinetic energy is not conserved. Therefore only momentum is conserved, which is option A.

fep-2d2a2b2fa2c542b5-q11:whole.hint: Sketch the initial and final vectors. A change is final minus initial, with the arrows still carrying direction.
notes: Calculate changes component by component: Δv = v_final − v_initial, or Δp = p_final − p_initial. Reversing direction requires a sign change.
An unchanged speed does not mean unchanged velocity. State both magnitude and direction when a vector is requested.

fep-2d2a2b2fa2c542b5-q13:whole.hint: Draw a force equation for each connected body, using compatible positive directions along the string.
notes: An inextensible taut string links the accelerations. A light string over an ideal pulley has the same tension on both sides.
To find acceleration, combine the equations to eliminate internal tension. Then substitute back into a single-body equation to find the tension.

duplicate-7a97a93853502f2e.hint: Isolate the named object. Add an arrow for each interaction it has with its surroundings.
notes: Draw only forces acting on this object: weight, contact force, tension, friction or other stated interactions. Label directions and place weight at the centre of mass.
The resultant is the vector sum of these forces. Do not add an extra “ma force” or put a Newton’s-third-law reaction on the same object.

fep-344c0cc5f6227b72-q9:whole.hint: Resolve forces parallel and perpendicular to the contact surface. Decide which way the object would tend to move.
notes: For a simple incline, weight has components mg sin θ down the plane and mg cos θ into it. Other applied forces can change the normal reaction.
Kinetic friction has magnitude μ_k N. Static friction adjusts up to μ_s N; use the maximum only at impending slip, and choose its direction to oppose relative slipping.

duplicate-d0639bd5d4636278.hint: Choose the object or system and identify the resultant force, rather than using one force on its own.
notes: Newton’s second law is ΣF = ma. Resolve into independent directions; zero acceleration requires zero resultant force in that direction.
Newton’s third-law forces act on different bodies and are the same kind of interaction. Balanced forces act on the same body.

duplicate-44a4f7365760cb5f.hint: Choose a system containing the interacting objects and compare its total momentum before and after the event.
notes: When external impulse is negligible, Σmu = Σmv. Keep velocity signs, and apply the equation separately in each direction for a two-dimensional collision.
“Sticks together” gives one shared final velocity. Kinetic energy is conserved only for an elastic collision; momentum conservation alone does not make a collision elastic.

duplicate-cfba9e2599088621.hint: Mark the centre of the circle. Which components of the real forces point towards it?
notes: Use ΣF_radial = mv²/r towards the centre. “Centripetal force” names this resultant; it is not an additional force.
At the top and bottom of a vertical circle the weight contributes with different radial signs. At loss of contact or a just-taut string, set the contact force or tension to zero.

fep-9f552d18c650a764-q2:whole.hint: Carry out the calculation without rounding, then compare the precision of the measurements used.
notes: The least precise relevant measurement limits the justified precision of a calculated result. Keep extra digits during intermediate steps.
Significant figures count from the first nonzero digit; they are not the same as decimal places. A more detailed calculator display is not a more accurate measurement.

fep-9f552d18c650a764-q6:whole.hint: Consider the momentum carried away or brought in by the mass flowing each second.
notes: Force is the rate of momentum change. For a stream brought to rest, its magnitude is mass flow rate multiplied by the change in velocity.
For density ρ, area A and speed v, mass flow rate is ρAv. Include direction and any incoming momentum when applying the relation to a nozzle or rocket.

fep-48711ac5ebc72e6f-q8:whole.text: D. Translational equilibrium requires zero resultant force. The object can be at rest or moving with constant velocity; equilibrium does not require zero velocity.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q11:whole.text: B. Newton’s third law gives equal-magnitude, opposite-direction interaction forces. The objects can have different accelerations because their masses differ.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q13:whole.text: A. The total momentum of Joe and the ball remains zero when external impulse is negligible: they acquire equal and opposite momenta. Their total kinetic energy increases because chemical energy is converted into motion.

fep-59e9fdff25044e14-q14:whole.text: C. Velocity is tangent to the circular path, upwards at the position shown. Acceleration points towards the centre, to the left. Constant speed does not mean zero acceleration.
